summary: Blackbushe Airport (BBS/EGLK) is a historic general aviation airfield on the Surrey/Hampshire border near Camberley, originally opened as RAF Hartford Bridge in 1942 and later renamed RAF Blackbushe. In the late 1940s and 1950s it briefly served as a major London-area airport before commercial traffic moved to Heathrow, and today it handles private pilots, flight training, business aviation and maintenance. Its main asphalt runway and VFR-friendly environment make it a popular base for light aircraft in the South East.
faqs:
Q: What are Blackbushe Airport's codes?
A: Its IATA code is BBS and its ICAO code is EGLK.

Q: Is Blackbushe open to general aviation?
A: Yes, it is a general aviation airfield welcoming private, training and business aircraft; check current PPR, handling and landing fee requirements before flight.

Q: What facilities are available at Blackbushe?
A: Fuel, flight training, maintenance, hangarage, a café and parking are typically available; confirm current hours and services before arrival.

Q: How far is Blackbushe from London?
A: It is about 40 miles (65 km) southwest of central London, roughly an hour by car depending on traffic, with convenient access from the M3 and A30.
transport_tips: By road, Blackbushe is just off the A30 near Yateley, with easy access from M3 junction 4A and parking on site. There is no direct rail link; the nearest stations include Blackwater, Fleet and Camberley, so plan a taxi or local bus for the final leg. If you are flying in, arrange handling, fuel and ground transport in advance, especially outside normal operating hours.
local_tip: If visiting on a Sunday, note that the long-running market can make the access road and car park busy; flyers should arrive early and always check the latest NOTAMs and noise abatement procedures.
